title: When infrastructure is not enough: understanding faculty intention towards AI adoption in a resource-constrained developing economy
abstract: Purpose Artificial intelligence (AI) offers transformative potential for higher education, yet faculty adoption in developing contexts remains underexplored. This study examines how personal innovativeness, facilities conditions, perceived usefulness and perceived ease of use influence faculty intention to adopt AI, with self-efficacy serving as a mediating mechanism, within the context of a resource-constrained developing economy. Design/methodology/approach A quantitative research design was adopted, underpinned by the positivism paradigm and a hypothetico-deductive method. Data were collected via a structured questionnaire from 388 faculty members across 10 private universities in Dhaka, Bangladesh. The data were analysed using Smart PLS 4.0 for structural equation modelling and SPSS v25 for preliminary statistical analysis. Findings Personal innovativeness, perceived usefulness, perceived ease of use and self-efficacy each show positive and significant relationships with intention to use AI. Personal innovativeness, facilities conditions and perceived usefulness are also found to have positive and significant relationships with intention to use AI through the mediating effect of self-efficacy, highlighting self-efficacy's central role in translating readiness and resources into adoption intention. Originality/value The study extends the technology acceptance model by integrating personal, institutional and cognitive factors into a single framework, offering theoretical contribution and practical guidance for policymakers seeking to improve AI adoption among faculty in resource-constrained higher education settings such as Bangladesh, where infrastructure alone proves insufficient to drive adoption.

title: Viscoelasticity of synthetic antigen presenting cells reprograms T cell metabolism for TCR-T cell manufacturing and therapy
abstract: Abstract Adoptive T cell receptor (TCR)–based immunotherapy offers a powerful strategy to target solid tumors. However, how the physical properties of the antigen-presenting interface regulate T cell metabolic programming remains poorly defined. Here we develop synthetic viscoelastic activating cells (SynVAC), artificial antigen-presenting cells whose stress-relaxation kinetics are chemically tuned independently of stiffness and of peptide–MHC (pMHC) and co-stimulatory ligand density. SynVAC-pMHC provides a defined, scalable platform that outperforms monocyte-derived dendritic cells to enrich antigen-specific CD8 + T cells. Fast-relaxing SynVAC-pMHC amplifies TCR signaling and mTOR activity, drives metabolic changes, and programs antigen-specific T cells toward an energetically favorable state with improved memory-like features after expansion. TCR-T cells expanded using fast-relaxing SynVAC-pMHC exhibit superior persistence and durable antitumor activity in melanoma and ovarian cancer models. These results establish cell-mimetic viscoelasticity as a key biophysical cue governing T cell metabolism and differentiation and offer a fully synthetic strategy for manufacturing potent TCR-T cells.

title: Uneven recovery: spatial and temporal patterns in owner-driven housing reconstruction after the 2015 Nepal Earthquake
journal: International Journal of Disaster Resilience in the Built Environment
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine whether urban disadvantage in post-earthquake housing reconstruction in Nepal is a general urban pattern or is concentrated within the Kathmandu Valley, and whether spatial disparities persisted over time. Design/methodology/approach Quarterly panel data from 131 municipalities across the 14 districts most severely affected by the 2015 Gorkha earthquake, covering November 2018 to November 2020, are analyzed. Pooled ordinary least squares (OLS) regression with municipality-clustered robust standard errors and period fixed effects models quarterly reconstruction flow rates using municipality type, lagged cumulative reconstruction progress, housing characteristics, poverty and other municipal characteristics. Additional robustness analyses assess the sensitivity of the findings to alternative model specifications. Findings Urban disadvantage is not uniform. Urban municipalities within the Kathmandu Valley had significantly lower quarterly reconstruction flow rates than rural municipalities, whereas urban municipalities outside the Valley showed no statistically significant difference. Lagged cumulative reconstruction progress was negatively associated with reconstruction flow, while the share of stone/mud-masonry housing showed a positive association. Reconstruction activity varied across periods, including a decline coinciding with the COVID-19 pandemic. Practical implications The observed spatial disparities highlight the importance of considering local reconstruction conditions when designing and delivering financial and technical assistance, particularly in dense and historically complex urban settings such as the Kathmandu Valley. Originality/value This municipality-level longitudinal analysis highlights important heterogeneity within urban areas, showing that reconstruction patterns vary not only between urban and rural municipalities but also across different urban contexts.

title: The voice–evidence gap: how reviews and surveys differ in the relational representation of customer satisfaction
abstract: Purpose Digital platforms now host massive volumes of consumer-generated content, and firms increasingly treat online reviews and structured surveys as parallel “listening systems” for assessing service quality and satisfaction. However, whether these sources can be used interchangeably as indicators of customer satisfaction remains an open empirical question. This study examines the voice–evidence gap by comparing how online reviews and survey responses represent satisfaction. Design/methodology/approach This study uses a network-based approach to examine how customer satisfaction is represented across different customer-information sources. Online reviews capture co-occurring experiential cues, whereas surveys record responses to pre-specified attributes. Study 1 analyzes 10,752 online reviews using a co-occurrence network, and Study 2 examines 506 survey responses using a partial correlation network. The study compares the relational structures derived from the two data sources. Findings The findings reveal a voice–evidence gap as an observed divergence in the relational representation of customer satisfaction across the two data sources. Customer satisfaction is embedded within clusters of co-mentioned experiential attributes in the review-based co-occurrence network but is less locally embedded within these clusters in the survey-based partial correlation network while maintaining strong overall network connectivity. In review-based networks, satisfaction aligns closely with hygiene and other experiential service cues. In survey-based networks, professionalism emerges as the principal bridging attribute linking experiential attributes to satisfaction. These findings show that relying on a single data source can yield incomplete representations of customer satisfaction. Originality/value This study contributes to marketing intelligence research by showing that consumer data sources differ not only in content but also in how they represent satisfaction relationally. By comparing relational structures across reviews and survey data, the study illustrates how different customer-information sources are associated with different relational representations of customer satisfaction.

title: Surgical treatment of pain syndrome in patients with amputation defects of the limbs resulting from combat trauma
journal: Bulletin of the Russian Military Medical Academy
abstract: BACKGROUND: Combat-related limb injury requiring amputation is a severe, disabling injury. Effective prosthetic fitting is key to the quality of life of such patients. One of the main obstacles to prosthetic fitting is chronic pain syndrome. AIM: To evaluate the efficacy of various surgical treatment methods for pain syndrome in patients with amputated limb defects resulting from combat trauma, and to identify factors influencing the treatment outcome. METHODS: Pain was assessed using a visual analog scale and a neuropathic pain diagnostic questionnaire. To identify independent predictors of failure in pain control, unsuccessful prosthetic fitting, and recurrence, a multivariable logistic regression analysis was performed. RESULTS: Neurosurgical operations using microsurgical techniques and the addition of alcohol neurolysis (chemical neurolysis with alcohol) were superior to similar operations without alcoholization. Thus, the median visual analog scale score after treatment was 0.5 points versus 1 point (p = 0.018), and the success rate of prosthetic fitting was 76% versus 53% (p = 0.022). In 66.7% of patients who underwent repeated surgeries, switching to neurosurgical interventions using microsurgical techniques and nerve alcoholization ensured successful prosthetic fitting. A correlation was identified between the time from injury to admission and the duration of treatment (r = 0.42; p = 0.004). Operations without nerve alcoholization were the strongest independent risk factor for failure in pain relief, unsuccessful prosthetic fitting, and recurrence (odds ratio = 5.05; p = 0.009; 5.81; p = 0.011; and 5.21; p = 0.015, respectively). Therapeutic blocks were associated with a lower risk of failure in pain relief and prosthetic fitting (odds ratio = 0.1; p = 0.040 and 0.06; p = 0.046, respectively). Amputation at the thigh level was a predictor of unsuccessful prosthetic fitting and recurrence (odds ratio = 4.18; p = 0.025 and 3.82; p = 0.036, respectively); each additional neuroma increased the risk of unsuccessful prosthetic fitting by 2.1-fold (p = 0.025) and the risk of recurrence by 2.41-fold (p = 0.012). CONCLUSION: Adding nerve alcoholization to microsurgical interventions significantly improves the outcomes of neuroma treatment and reduces the risk of recurrence; surgeries without nerve alcoholization are not recommended as a standalone method for this population. The identified predictors can be used for risk stratification, but they require confirmation in larger samples.
